title: ticfac watch: the whole epic at a glance, attention first, live in place
description:
OPERATOR, 2026-09-23, after working it through from first principles: 'it should visualize progress over the entire epic, so also completed waves and upcoming waves' - and 'something simple that doesn't assume a pane size'.

A RENDERER of the model in 6dh (ticfac status --json). It answers, in this order: does anything need me; is it healthy; how far along the whole epic; what is happening now; what happened and what is next.

LESSONS TAKEN:
  - Claude Code's todo list: the whole plan always visible; items never move, only their mark changes.
  - gh run watch: refresh in place; --compact one line per job when tall.
  - BuildKit / docker compose: fixed rows with live timers; log lines ABOVE, status below.
  - Turborepo / Nx full-screen TUIs: users call Turbo's 'really hard to use' - running tasks lost among finished ones, no native scrollback/copy/select - and fall back to stream mode. So: NO alternate screen.

LAYOUT:
  - an attention line at the top only when a person is needed: what, and the command that does it
  - per epic, the lifecycle as the progress bar: plan - waves k/n - review - close-out - merge, with elapsed and cost
  - the whole epic always visible, compressed by distance from now: done waves one line each; the ACTIVE wave expanded, one fixed row per tick; upcoming waves one dim line each
  - stable positions: a tick never moves, its mark changes; absorbed ticks appear as marked new rows; try history as marks (a failed try then a running one)
  - liveness as a signal: 'quiet N m' since the runner's last turn, amber then red
  - fits the pane: narrow drops columns (last turn first, then model), short collapses to '+N running'
  - no alternate screen: scrollback, copy, select and links keep working; not a TTY -> plain appended lines

OPEN, for the operator later: cost on screen (proposed yes, in the header), remaining time (only when measured), an alert when 'needs you' appears (bell or ticfac herd notify).
notes:
2026-09-23 14:25 - OPERATOR, 2026-09-23, clarifying the shape: 'for watch i would like it to not just scroll updates, but rather have a status per executor/tick in a fixed location'.

So: a LIVE BLOCK REDRAWN IN PLACE (the docker compose up / BuildKit progress pattern), not a stream of lines.
  - one row per tick/executor at a FIXED position, updated in place: state, try, tier/model, elapsed, silence, the last runner turn; new ticks add rows, finished ticks settle and stay
  - a header row per run above its ticks: what the run waits on and since when
  - nothing scrolls by default; an optional quiet line ABOVE the block for events worth keeping (a gate failed, a finding drafted) - log lines above, status below
  - height-aware: more rows than the terminal is tall -> active rows first, then '+N more'
  - width-aware: rows truncate/reflow to the pane; no fixed size assumed
  - only when stdout is not a TTY: plain appended lines
acceptance_criteria: ticfac watch renders the status model in place with no alternate screen: a top line only when a person is needed, naming the unblocking command; per epic the lifecycle as a progress bar with elapsed and cost; done waves one line each, the active wave one fixed row per tick, upcoming waves one line each; rows never reorder; per-tick silence shown as a colour-graded timer; it fits the pane's width and height as described; and when stdout is not a TTY it streams plain lines
